title: Questions during reading or after
statement: Whether checks belong during reading or after is unsettled: tests between parts of a recorded lecture improved recall, but in one study inferential questions during reading cut young readers' recall.
example: In one study, inferential questions during reading cut grade-4 recall from .30 to .07.
detail: A design review of a reading lesson flagged as its biggest cross-lesson implication a published study in which interpolated inferential questions cut grade-4 recall from .30 to .07; the review asked for questions after reading, not during it, and the project logged it as needing a ruling rather than acting alone (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0218-devfactory-review-and-decision-brief-2026-09-10.qmd`; van den Broek et al. 2001, https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-0663.93.3.521). In recorded lectures, interpolated memory tests cut mind-wandering by roughly a third and improved recall (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0248-g9-video-research-full-files.qmd`; Szpunar, Khan & Schacter 2013, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1221764110). The reading figure is for grade 4, and that study varied both grade and timing. To settle it: the same text with checks during and after reading, compared on later recall at more than one grade.

evidence.quote: interpolated inferential questions cut grade-4 recall .30->.07
Interpolated memory tests inserted into recorded lectures cut mind-wandering by roughly a third and improved recall versus uninterrupted video.
potential class risk for every arc's mid-passage checks including ours

evidence.quote: One idea per segment. Pause-to-check questions after the key segments. A spoken summary at the end.
Love the spot checks across the course of the reading to make sure it’s cohesive, but really cool if kids could listen to it as it’s going through.
Every video carries exactly one quick check, and it fires at the very end, never mid-clip: a video is watched through before it is checked, not interrupted to be checked.
